title: Attenuated hypothalamic response to fructose via a dedicated gut-brain pathway
title_zh: 通过专属肠脑通路介导的低反应性下丘脑反应于果糖
abstract: Fructose is a simple sugar and a major component of our diet, yet its effects on gut-brain feeding circuits remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how fructose influences activity in hypothalamic agouti-related protein (AgRP) neurons-key regulators of hunger. Fructose was markedly less effective than equicaloric glucose at suppressing AgRP neuron activity in mice, challenging the prevailing model of AgRP neurons as indiscriminate calorie detectors. This blunted neural response to fructose did not alter short-term food consumption but was instructive for food preference, demonstrating that graded AgRP neuron activity changes are sufficient to guide food choice. Mechanistically, we discovered that fructose activates a distinct gut-brain pathway involving the release of PYY and signaling through Y2 receptor-expressing vagal afferent neurons to inhibit AgRP neurons. These findings unexpectedly reveal that AgRP neurons respond not just to calories, but to specific nutrients, and highlight how fructose engages a unique gut-brain pathway to communicate with AgRP neurons.
abstract_zh: 果糖是简单糖，也是饮食中的主要成分，但其对肠脑进食通路的作用尚不清楚。我们在此研究了果糖如何影响下丘脑AgRP神经元活动——这些神经元是饥饿的关键调节器。与等热量葡萄糖相比，果糖明显不易抑制小鼠AgRP神经元活动，这对“AgRP神经元仅作为非选择性热量探测器”的既有模型提出挑战。对果糖反应的钝化并未改变短期食量，但会影响食物偏好，表明分级的AgRP神经元活动变化足以指导食物选择。机制上，我们发现果糖激活了一条独特的肠脑通路：通过PYY释放并经Y2受体表达的迷走传入神经元信号，进而抑制AgRP神经元。这些结果意外地表明AgRP神经元不仅对热量作出反应，还对特定营养素作出反应，并凸显果糖通过独特肠脑通路与AgRP神经元沟通。
